status: Closed — sealed candidate ownership regression verified on 2026-09-02
finding: Commit candidate resolution expands from the task's declared scope paths into dirty source bytes currently owned by another active claim. A narrow claim or explicit --files selection does not narrow this candidate, so the current task can become responsible for another lane's unfinished bytes and then cannot release without ATM_RELEASE_DIRTY_WIP_BLOCKED.
expectedBehavior: A task-scoped commit candidate must be derived from task-owned delivery intent plus ownership-attributed changes, not from every dirty path matching a broad card scope. Foreign active dirty bytes must remain outside the candidate and be reported as an overlap diagnostic; only a true semantic dependency may require compose/revalidation or a short queue boundary.
evidenceOrRepro: Observed on 2026-08-12 in the shared canonical worktree: an active claim over a card whose scopePaths included a source file being edited by another lane absorbed that dirty file into candidate resolution even when the claimant used a narrowed file set. Release then failed with ATM_RELEASE_DIRTY_WIP_BLOCKED and every offered recovery path required mutating the foreign bytes. Detailed command receipts remain available from the reporting captain.
followUp: Resolved by the sealed commit candidate authority path. packages/cli/src/commands/git-governance/implementation/commit-bundle-resolution.test.ts was rerun on 2026-09-02: its broad-scope/narrow-claim two-lane fixture proves foreign active dirty bytes remain outside the current task's candidate, while released residue is preserved rather than mutated. The test passed.
